item.title: Eurobites: Huawei builds backbone in South Africa
item.description: Also in today's EMEA regional roundup: X bites back; EU probes Google over AI shenanigans; Openreach bags former Truespeed boss.

item.title: Broadband consultants push for BEAD 'rainy day fund'
item.description: To prepare for anticipated cost overruns with BEAD builds, and to connect locations left behind by RDOF defaults, Vernonburg Group is recommending the NTIA create a $6 billion 'rainy day fund' from BEAD's remaining $21 billion.

item.title: Comcast's bid for Warner Bros. was cash-light
item.description: As the Warner Bros. Discovery saga turns toward Netflix's initial winning bid and Paramount Skydance's hostile offer, Comcast President Mike Cavanagh discussed why Comcast bid and where it likely came up short.

item.title: Tom Rutledge nets 2026 Bresnan Ethics in Business Award
item.description: The Syndeo Institute at The Cable Center has named industry vet Tom Rutledge as the 2026 Bresnan Ethics in Business Award Winner. He'll be honored at the 2026 Cable Hall of Fame gala next April. #pressrelease

item.title: FWA product is improving, but AT&T still 'fiber first' – Stankey
item.description: AT&T is preaching quality over quantity for its growing Internet Air fixed wireless access product. But fiber 'is fundamental and foundational to this business,' says CEO John Stankey.

item.title: Ofcom hails lift-off for D2D satellite services in the UK
item.description: Ofcom paves the way for UK operators to form satco partnerships and launch D2D services in existing mobile spectrum bands.

item.title: T-Mobile disables automated switching app for AT&T customers
item.description: T-Mobile stops automated version of Easy Switch for AT&T customers after legal challenge, while Verizon says the tool raises customer privacy concerns.

item.title: US PC shipments see 1% annual drop for a second consecutive quarter – Omdia
item.description: Omdia's outlook for the holiday season remains positive and the US PC market is still expected to grow in 2025, with full-year shipments forecast to increase by 4%.

item.title: Mediacom bows low-cost broadband for first responders
item.description: Mediacom has introduced a $29.99 per month broadband option for first responders that's backed by a five-year price lock. #pressrelease

item.title: Charter's streaming app offer for pay-TV subs 'not a gimmick' – CEO
item.description: Charter's new app store enables pay-TV subs to install a range of video streaming apps for no added cost. Initial uptake is promising, but adoption will rise as more customers realize 'it's not a gimmick,' CEO Chris Winfrey says.
